newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mostly up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates, spots end mostly up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Monday with institutions borrowing on the repo market due an active domestic A share market, traders said.
Turnover rose to 6.95 million lots from 4.53 million last Friday. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.

But the annual rate for the most active seven-day contract bucked the trend and slipped to 7.36 percent from 8.90 percent with investors returning to the repo market short-term money borrowed for two new A share issues last week, traders said.
Both Shanghai and Shenzhen A share markets surged today in very active trading, continuing a bull run that began in April mainly on official Beijing support for the securities market.

An A share company, Tibet Shendi, will be listed in Shanghai on Tuesday and another, Qinghai Tongren Aluminum Industrial Co, will issue shares on Wednesday, leading institutions to borrow money on the repo market, traders said.
Traders expect the rates to stand firm in the next few trading days.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on a rise in the most active 10-year bond, traders said.
The 10-year bond that matures in June 2006, regarded as a market barometer, rose to 122.93 yuan from 122.15.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market increased to 3.14 million lots from 1.75 million with trading volume in the 10-year bond accounting for nearly two-thirds of the total.
Traders said the rise in the 10-year bond on heavy volume might herald a recovery of the T-bill spot market in the short term after weeks of falls.
